newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes puts protest cost at 220 mln dmks.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes puts protest cost at 220 mln dmks.

text.p: Daimler-Benz AG's Mercedes luxury car-making unit Mercedes on Tuesday estimated that the total cost to the company of stoppages by workers to protest against sick pay cuts amounted to 220 million marks.

A Mercedes spokesman said by telephone that protests by thousands of employees at plants across the country earlier on Tuesday had cost the company around 80 million marks, adding to the 140 million marks of costs resulting from stoppages over the last week.
He added that in total some 4,000 vehicles fewer had been produced.

The Mercedes figures largely corroborate estimates given earlier on Tuesday by worker representatives at Mercedes' Daimler-Benz parent company. They calculated costs in the region of 200 million marks and said 4-5,000 units of production had been lost.

No official estimate has yet been given for the total cost of the protests to the Daimler-Benz group, which was the first large company to announce last week that it would be implementing a new law allowing it to cut sick pay immediately.
According to Daimler's work council, around 100,000 workers will by the end of the night shift have stopped on Tuesday work to protest against the decision.
